Formulation
John Doe experienced anxiety due to an insect sting, leading to a localized allergic reaction. Anxiety is exacerbated by the fear of severe allergic reaction. No history of serious allergic reactions or anaphylaxis is noted.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Anxiety related to insect sting
- Patient Goal(s): Reduce anxiety and manage reaction to insect sting
- Clinical Goal(s): Educate on allergic reactions and manage anxiety symptoms
- Actions (Patient): Take over-the-counter antihistamines as needed; Monitor the sting site and seek further help if symptoms worsen
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Provide reassurance; Educate on signs of severe reactions; Provide information link on anaphylaxis

Secondary Problem: Localized allergic reaction
- Patient Goal(s): Manage localized reaction and prevent progression
- Clinical Goal(s): Monitor for escalation; Prescribe antibiotics if infection signs appear
- Actions (Patient): Use antihistamines; Seek medical attention if reactions escalate
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Educate patient on symptoms, monitor through follow-up if necessary

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Insect sting reactions, use of antihistamines, monitoring for escalation
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Swelling of lips, breathing difficulty, rash spreading
- Coping Strategies: Use of antihistamines, contact healthcare providers for reassurance
